summary: The study fabricated delaminated Ti3C2Tx nanopapers and Ti3C2Tx/carboxymethylated-CNF composites by aqueous mixing and vacuum filtration, with some composites subsequently vacuum pressed. It also fabricated Ti3C2Tx/CNC comparison composites and a pristine CNF reference paper; these did not have reported electrochemical capacitances. Electrochemical paper-electrode data were explicitly reported for pristine Ti3C2Tx and 5%, 10%, and 20% CNF composites in 3 m sulfuric acid; Ti3C2Tx–10% CNF is the headline multifunctional electrode, while the highest explicitly printed gravimetric capacitance was 369 F g−1 for Ti3C2Tx–5% CNF at 2 mV s−1. Major data gaps are mass loading, BET/porosity/pore size, and numerical capacitances for the 40–80% CNF, CNC, and vacuum-pressed variants.
